overall_findings.statement: Reduced throughput alongside increased frame loss was identified in 3 configuration(s): 120 Mbps (90/10), 160 Mbps (70/30), 160 Mbps (90/10).
Increased latency without observed frame loss was identified in 3 configuration(s): 80 Mbps (70/30), 80 Mbps (90/10), 120 Mbps (70/30).
Increased latency without clear evidence of throughput degradation was identified in 3 configuration(s): 80 Mbps (70/30), 80 Mbps (90/10), 120 Mbps (70/30).
Detected degradation without detected improvement was identified in 6 configuration(s): 80 Mbps (70/30), 80 Mbps (90/10), 120 Mbps (70/30), 120 Mbps (90/10), 160 Mbps (70/30), 160 Mbps (90/10).
Imbalance-induced theoretical overload was identified in 3 configuration(s): 120 Mbps (90/10), 160 Mbps (70/30), 160 Mbps (90/10).
No theoretical link overload was identified in 6 configuration(s): 80 Mbps (50/50), 80 Mbps (70/30), 80 Mbps (90/10), 120 Mbps (50/50), 120 Mbps (70/30), 160 Mbps (50/50).

limitations: The simulation models two independent Ethernet links with fixed traffic assignments.
Dynamic traffic redistribution and link aggregation hashing are not modeled.
Results apply to the simulated configurations and may not generalize to physical networks.
Confidence intervals are individual 95% intervals without adjustment for multiple comparisons.
Inconclusive comparisons do not establish equivalent performance.
Theoretical capacity limits do not establish the exact experimental onset of frame loss.
Performance extremes describe observed means and do not necessarily establish statistically supported differences.
